addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Now I have the complete picture. Here is my comprehensive report.

---

## Project Overview

This is **Memos** (`github.com/usememos/memos`), a self-hosted, open-source memo/note-taking application written in Go. It uses a multi-database architecture supporting SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL through a `Driver` interface pattern.

## Data Layer Location

The data layer lives entirely in the **`/bench/home/work/store/`** directory, in the Go package `store` (module path `github.com/usememos/memos/store`). The data layer is organized as:

- **Entity definitions and store methods**: top-level `.go` files in `/bench/home/work/store/`
- **Driver interface**: `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go`
- **Database-specific implementations**: `/bench/home/work/store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`
- **Migrations**: `/bench/home/work/store/migration/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`
- **Protobuf payload/setting definitions**: `/bench/home/work/proto/store/` (proto definitions) and `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/` (generated Go code)

## All Persistent Entity Types

There are **12 persistent entity types** (corresponding to 12 database tables). Each struct is defined in `package store` (`github.com/usememos/memos/store`):

### 1. User
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/user.go`
- **Struct**: `User`
- **DB Table**: `user`
- **Fields**: ID, RowStatus, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Username, Role, Email, Nickname, PasswordHash, AvatarURL, Description
- **Related types**: `UpdateUser`, `FindUser`, `DeleteUser`, `Role` (enum: ADMIN, USER)

### 2. Memo
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go`
- **Struct**: `Memo`
- **DB Table**: `memo`
- **Fields**: ID, UID, RowStatus, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Content, Visibility, Pinned, Payload (protobuf `MemoPayload`), ParentUID (composed)
- **Related types**: `FindMemo`, `FindMemoPayload`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `Visibility` (enum: PUBLIC, PROTECTED, PRIVATE)

### 3. Attachment
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go`
- **Struct**: `Attachment`
- **DB Table**: `attachment`
- **Fields**: ID, UID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Filename, Blob, Type, Size, StorageType (protobuf enum), Reference, Payload (protobuf `AttachmentPayload`), MemoID
- **Related types**: `FindAttachment`, `UpdateAttachment`, `DeleteAttachment`

### 4. MemoRelation
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/memo_relation.go`
- **Struct**: `MemoRelation`
- **DB Table**: `memo_relation`
- **Fields**: MemoID, RelatedMemoID, Type
- **Related types**: `FindMemoRelation`, `DeleteMemoRelation`, `MemoRelationType` (enum: REFERENCE, COMMENT)

### 5. MemoShare
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/memo_share.go`
- **Struct**: `MemoShare`
- **DB Table**: `memo_share`
- **Fields**: ID, UID, MemoID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, ExpiresTs
- **Related types**: `FindMemoShare`, `DeleteMemoShare`

### 6. IdentityProvider
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/idp.go`
- **Struct**: `IdentityProvider`
- **DB Table**: `idp`
- **Fields**: ID, UID, Name, Type (protobuf `IdentityProvider_Type`), IdentifierFilter, Config (JSON string)
- **Related types**: `FindIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProviderV1`, `DeleteIdentityProvider`

### 7. Inbox
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/inbox.go`
- **Struct**: `Inbox`
- **DB Table**: `inbox`
- **Fields**: ID, CreatedTs, SenderID, ReceiverID, Status, Message (protobuf `InboxMessage`)
- **Related types**: `UpdateInbox`, `FindInbox`, `DeleteInbox`, `InboxStatus` (enum: UNREAD, ARCHIVED)

### 8. Reaction
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/reaction.go`
- **Struct**: `Reaction`
- **DB Table**: `reaction`
- **Fields**: ID, CreatedTs, CreatorID, ContentID, ReactionType
- **Related types**: `FindReaction`, `DeleteReaction`

### 9. InstanceSetting (a.k.a. SystemSetting)
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/instance_setting.go`
- **Struct**: `InstanceSetting`
- **DB Table**: `system_setting`
- **Fields**: Name, Value, Description
- **Related types**: `FindInstanceSetting`, `DeleteInstanceSetting`
- **Note**: The raw `InstanceSetting` struct maps to the `system_setting` table. It is converted to/from the protobuf `storepb.InstanceSetting` which has typed keys (BASIC, GENERAL, STORAGE, MEMO_RELATED, TAGS, NOTIFICATION, AI).

### 10. UserSetting
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/user_setting.go`
- **Struct**: `UserSetting`
- **DB Table**: `user_setting`
- **Fields**: UserID, Key (protobuf `UserSetting_Key`), Value (JSON string)
- **Related types**: `FindUserSetting`, `DeleteUserSetting`, `RefreshTokenQueryResult`, `PATQueryResult`
- **Note**: The Value field stores JSON-serialized protobuf payloads. The Key enum covers: SHORTCUTS, GENERAL, TAGS, REFRESH_TOKENS, PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKENS, WEBHOOKS.

### 11. UserIdentity
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/user_identity.go`
- **Struct**: `UserIdentity`
- **DB Table**: `user_identity`
- **Fields**: ID, UserID, Provider, ExternUID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs
- **Related types**: `FindUserIdentity`, `DeleteUserIdentity`

### 12. DeleteUserResult (auxiliary/transactional)
- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/user_delete.go`
- **Struct**: `DeleteUserResult`
- **Not a table itself**, but a transactional result type returned when deleting a User, containing the collected `Attachments` and `UserSettingKeys` that were removed.

## Supporting Types (not separate tables, but foundational)

- **`RowStatus`** (enum: NORMAL, ARCHIVED) -- defined in `/bench/home/work/store/common.go`
- **`Store`** (the main store facade) -- defined in `/bench/home/work/store/store.go`
- **`Driver`** (interface for all DB backends) -- defined in `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go`
- **`AuthenticationConfigState`** and **`AuthenticationConfigMutation`** -- defined in `/bench/home/work/store/auth_config.go`, used for atomic authentication config mutations across InstanceSetting and IdentityProvider tables.
- **`deploymentConfiguration`** -- defined in `/bench/home/work/store/deployment_config.go`, an in-memory struct for file-backed configuration (not persisted to DB itself).

## Protobuf Payload Definitions

Several entities store rich payloads as JSON-serialized protobuf messages. The proto source files are at:

- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto` -- `MemoPayload`
- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/attachment.proto` -- `AttachmentPayload`, `AttachmentStorageType`
- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/idp.proto` -- `IdentityProvider`, `OAuth2Config`
- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/inbox.proto` -- `InboxMessage`
- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/instance_setting.proto` -- `InstanceSetting` and all sub-settings
- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/user_setting.proto` -- `UserSetting` and all sub-settings

## Summary Table

| # | Entity Type | Go Struct | DB Table | Definition File |
|---|-------------|-----------|----------|-----------------|
| 1 | User | `User` | `user` | `store/user.go` |
| 2 | Memo | `Memo` | `memo` | `store/memo.go` |
| 3 | Attachment | `Attachment` | `attachment` | `store/attachment.go` |
| 4 | MemoRelation | `MemoRelation` | `memo_relation` | `store/memo_relation.go` |
| 5 | MemoShare | `MemoShare` | `memo_share` | `store/memo_share.go` |
| 6 | IdentityProvider | `IdentityProvider` | `idp` | `store/idp.go` |
| 7 | Inbox | `Inbox` | `inbox` | `store/inbox.go` |
| 8 | Reaction | `Reaction` | `reaction` | `store/reaction.go` |
| 9 | InstanceSetting | `InstanceSetting` | `system_setting` | `store/instance_setting.go` |
| 10 | UserSetting | `UserSetting` | `user_setting` | `store/user_setting.go` |
| 11 | UserIdentity | `UserIdentity` | `user_identity` | `store/user_identity.go` |

All entity types live in Go package `store` (import path `github.com/usememos/memos/store`). All file paths above are relative to `/bench/home/work/`. The canonical schema covering all 11 tables is at `/bench/home/work/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`.

input.command:
# For each persistent entity type, count how many distinct Go packages outside store/ reference it
# We'll search for store.EntityType patterns in Go files outside the store/ directory

entities=("User" "Memo" "Attachment" "MemoRelation" "MemoShare" "IdentityProvider" "Inbox" "Reaction" "InstanceSetting" "UserSetting" "UserIdentity")

for entity in "${entities[@]}"; do
    # Find distinct packages (directories) that reference store.$entity
    count=$(grep -rl "store\.\(${entity}\b\|Find${entity}\b\|Update${entity}\b\|Delete${entity}\b\)" --include='*.go' . \
        | grep -v '^\./store/' \
        | grep -v '^\./vendor/' \
        | grep -v '^\./graphify-out/' \
        | sed 's|/[^/]*$||' \
        | sort -u \
        | wc -l)
    echo "$entity: $count packages"
done
